transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I came in because my mind is just... constantly jumping from one thing to another. Like, I work in a lab, and I'm always worrying about whether our new partnership is going to cut my position, or if my data is wrong. 

And then it just shifts to whether my bills are going to pile up, or worrying that my family thinks I'm falling behind... or if I've already ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It's just constant, and I can't really seem to shut it off.
Have you had any recent changes in your physical health, such as thyroid problems, heart issues, or have you started any new medications or supplements recently?

No, um... no physical changes that I know of. I haven't had any thyroid or heart problems, or anything like that. And I haven't started taking any new medications or... supplements recently, either. Physically, as far as I know, everything is pretty much normal.
How long have you been experiencing these constant worries and racing thoughts that you can't turn off?

It's been about seven months now. It started right around the time our lab had a major funding shift. We got this new commercial partnership, and it really changed how everything was being run. Ever since then, the worrying just hasn't stopped.
Besides the constant worrying, have you noticed any physical symptoms like muscle tension, difficulty sleeping, or feeling restless or on edge?

Yeah, definitely. Um, especially at work. I just feel really... wound up, I guess? Like I can't even settle into my chair. I end up just tapping my foot constantly, or I'm always checking my messages. Sometimes I'll just walk back to the instrument room for no reason at all, just because I can't sit still. And I've noticed I get startled really easily, too... like just normal lab noises, a door shutting or something, and I jump. It's just this really on-edge feeling all the time.
When you feel that wound-up, on-edge feeling, does it come on suddenly and intensely, like it peaks within a few minutes? Or is it more of a constant background anxiety throughout the day?
It's definitely more of a constant background thing. It doesn't really come on all at once or peak quickly like that. It's just... always there, humming in the background, pretty much all day long.
